articles.content: The headline jump is largely priced in, so the market reaction will hinge on core. A print at the top of the forecast range, around 0.24% or higher, would back the Fed officials warning that inflation is broadening and firm December hike pricing, lifting front-end yields and the dollar. A reading at the soft end, near 0.16% to 0.18%, would support New York Fed President Williams’ view that price pressures are shock-driven and could trim expectations for tightening beyond this year. For oil, the report is a reminder that crude is now feeding straight into US inflation through gasoline. Any renewed spike in prices from Gulf escalation would show up in next month’s headline and keep energy at the centre of the Fed debate. --- Earlier: US CPI: Energy prices expected to lift headline inflation. Will core stay contained? US CPI preview: energy set to lift inflation to 3.7%, core seen steady at 2.4% MUFG: US CPI seen at 3.6%, core must surprise to revive an October Fed hike --- Gasoline will do the heavy lifting in today’s US headline inflation, but the Fed’s next move depends on whether core stays as calm as Wall Street expects. Summary: US CPI for September is due Wednesday at 1230 GMT (0830 US Eastern) The median forecast from 14 forecasters, compiled by The Wall Street Journal, sees headline CPI up around 0.6% m/m and 3.6% y/y, from 0.4% and 3.4% in August Core is seen rising 0.22% m/m, down from 0.29%, with annual core at 2.4% Core forecasts range from 0.16% at Deutsche Bank to 0.24% at Goldman Sachs, Barclays and Morgan Stanley Forecasters are split almost evenly on whether annual core holds at 2.4% or edges up to 2.5% The Fed’s Beige Book follows later on Wednesday, ahead of the October 27-28 policy meeting US consumer prices are expected to post a sharp energy-driven rise in September, while underlying inflation is forecast to cool, according to a survey of Wall Street forecasters compiled by The Wall Street Journal ahead of Wednesday’s release at 1230 GMT (0830 US Eastern). The median forecast across 14 forecasters points to a rise of around 0.6% in headline CPI for the month, up from 0.4% in August, lifting the annual rate to 3.6% from 3.4%. Core prices, which exclude food and energy, are seen rising 0.22%, slower than August’s 0.29%, leaving the annual core rate at 2.4%. The headline boost reflects gasoline. US pump prices averaged above $4.30 a gallon in September, a record for the month, as the war involving Iran keeps crude prices high. Headline forecasts are tightly grouped, with Morgan Stanley at the top on a monthly basis and JPMorgan slightly below the pack. The core picture is less settled. Deutsche Bank has the softest call at 0.16%, with Citigroup and JPMorgan both at 0.18%, while Goldman Sachs, Barclays and Morgan Stanley sit at 0.24%. The difference matters for the annual rate: roughly half of forecasters, including Bank of America, Goldman Sachs, Barclays and Morgan Stanley, expect core to edge up to 2.5% year on year, while the rest, including Citigroup, Deutsche Bank and JPMorgan, see it holding at 2.4%. Part of the expected cooling reflects a one-off. Barclays and Morgan Stanley have noted that an unusual jump in wireless phone service prices lifted August’s core reading by around 0.1 percentage point and should partly unwind. The release lands as Fed officials debate whether inflation is broadening. On Tuesday, Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin said inflation is proving enduring, and Boston Fed President Susan Collins said she is watching how widespread price pressures are. New York Fed President John Williams argued the economy is not overheating. A firm core print would strengthen the first camp. A soft one would support Williams’ view that the pressure stems from specific shocks. There is also a measurement wrinkle. Core CPI has recently been running below core PCE, the Fed’s preferred gauge, which stood near 3% in August, so a benign core CPI print may flatter the measure the Fed actually targets. The Fed’s Beige Book follows later on Wednesday, ahead of the October 27-28 policy meeting, where markets currently expect the central bank to hold before a December hike. This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

articles.title: Nigeria: Economic Community of West African States (Ecowas) Commission and Denmark Kick Off Partnership on Increased Trade and Regional Economic Integration
articles.desc: The Increased Trade and Regional Economic Integration in Africa (ITREIA) project, which is anchored within the Department of Economic Affairs and Agriculture, aims to strengthen the Commission’s capacity and regional coordination to enhance cross-border trade, remove non-tariff barriers, and acceler
articles.content: The Increased Trade and Regional Economic Integration in Africa (ITREIA) project, which is anchored within the Department of Economic Affairs and Agriculture, aims to strengthen the Commission’s capacity and regional coordination to enhance cross-border trade, remove non-tariff barriers, and accelerate market integration across West Africa. The ITREIA programme directly supports Pillar 3 of the ECOWAS Vision 2050, which focuses on regional interconnectivity and economic integration, and targets three core outcome areas: intra-regional trade growth, reduction of non-tariff barriers and market competitiveness. In her remarks, Ms. Julie Rosenkilde HANNIBAL, Deputy Head of Mission at the Embassy of Denmark to Nigeria, reiterated Denmark’s commitment to supporting West Africa’s economic integration agenda, noting that robust institutional frameworks and streamlined market access are pivotal drivers of regional stability. Mr. Kolawole SOFOLA, Director of Trade at the ECOWAS Commission, in his remarks on behalf of the Commissioner for Economic Affairs and Agriculture, Mr. Dehpue ZUO, appreciated the Danish Government for its partnership and support towards empowering the Commission in its goal of improving economic growth and livelihoods of citizens in West Africa. Following the formal finalization of the bilateral agreement in August 2026, the kick-off session presented key operational procedures for programme execution. Deliberations covered project governance, financial management protocols, reporting schedules, the recruitment of an inception consultant and the composition of the dedicated Project Implementation Unit (PIU). Distributed by APO Group on behalf of Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS).

articles.title: OM System OM-1 Mark II Review
articles.desc: In 2026, there are legitimate reasons for you to choose another sensor format over Full Frame – be it larger one or, like in the case of Olympus - smaller. Olympus – the pioneers of the Micro Four Thirds system – are back in the camera business, and are now called OM System. But while their name has
articles.content: In 2026, there are legitimate reasons for you to choose another sensor format over Full Frame – be it larger one or, like in the case of Olympus - smaller. Olympus – the pioneers of the Micro Four Thirds system – are back in the camera business, and are now called OM System. But while their name has changed, everything else in terms of the promise is what they are looking to deliver with their latest – the OM-1 Mark II. Priced at ₹2.3L (body only), it is entering an arena filled with ever existing strong players – with a desire to hold its own. In this review we dig into the system, to see what it offers and why your next adventure camera could be a micro four thirds. OM-1 Mark II Look, Body, Feel The OM-1 Mark II at first glance looks and feels almost like a full-frame body, it weighs right at 511 grams and feels comfortable. It is similar in size to Sony’s A7 IV – which is a global bestseller – but the differences pop out immediately when you start handling it. The button layout is different as compared to other systems which means there is a learning curve to ensure you don’t hit the wrong button. You have all the familiar buttons & dials – and most of these are customisable, but one thing to note is the the video record button in photo mode serves the purpose of turning on the Hi-res mode – and this can be annoying if it gets toggled by accident, which happened with us a bunch of times. The back of the camera features buttons that are familiar and fall immediately within muscle memory but according to us, the ISO button on the top right could have better placement and isn’t the most ergonomic. What’s unique about this body is that OM System claims the weather sealing of this body and specifies that it is dustproof, freezeproof and splashproof – which is important for a rugged body suitable for outdoor adventures. This is also evident with the I/O ports – audio input & output jacks, as well USB-C and a micro HDMI port – covered with high quality rubber covers; And the right side of the body features dual SD card slots, but no CF-Express slot like other cameras in the segment are starting to offer nowadays. OM-1 Mark II Features 20.4 MP stacked BSI CMOS Micro Four Thirds Sensor with TruPic X Processor 5-axis IBIS with up to 8.5 EV stops of stabilisation 14-bit RAW shooting capability Computational photography modes like Live ND, GND and Hi-res (50MP & 80MP) Up to 120fps using electronic shutter OM-1 Mark II Sensor and Image Quality Performance As an ode to the company’s history, we’re reviewing this camera body with a legacy Olympus M.Zuiko Digital 300mm F/4 IS Pro lens, which gives us an FF equivalent FOV of 600mm, as well as a newer M.Zuiko Digital 12-40mm F/2.8 II Pro lens (24-80mm FF equivalent). Quality-wise, the images showcase adequate dynamic range and colour tones appear natural without much processing, when shot in the Natural mode. Daylight shots can certainly be used straight out of the camera, and there are several interesting colour modes to choose from, which are also customisable. The lowlight ones aren’t as poppy and would definitely require work after. When switching on the burst mode, this camera can shoot 10 FPS with the mechanical shutter or 50fps with full tracking C-AF or 120 FPS with single-AF using the electronic shutter, but the buffer size inside this camera is just over 250 images. Unfortunately, since this camera only supports SD cards, the buffer is lower as compared to other cameras, but adequate; but you might feel that pinch in high-octane moments like in sports or wildlife for which this camera is designed. The plus point is that the buffer gets emptied rather quickly so to match that performance, we’d recommend getting a high speed UHS-II SD card. Another standout feature is that you can shoot at high burst rates, but also limit the number of shots you’re taking at one time, saving memory space as well as clearing the buffer faster. The computational photography modes set this camera apart from anything we've seen from other brands. You also have the option to toggle the live view mode on while using the ND filters or Graduated ND filters. The high resolution mode has two options for you to shoot with – One is handheld and gives you a 50 MP output and the other requires a tripod, but can give you an 80 MP output. Both of these image outputs are saved with a different raw format, so it becomes easier for you to find and process them afterwards. On that note, when you switch on highres mode, the camera takes a couple more seconds to process the image before showing you a preview and gets ready to shoot the next shot. So we would advise to use this mode for still images or for shooting landscapes for subjects that are not in motion. Another thing to note is that in the photography mode, the video recording button toggles the high resolution mode, so beware of shooting in critical conditions and not accidentally turning it on. OM-1 Mark II Autofocus The OM-1 Mark II has 1053 cross-type phase detection and contrast detection autofocus points. There are a multitude of AF modes to choose from including continuous AF tracking (C-AF TR) mode, which is separate from the C-AF mode. The focus acquisition is very quick and the camera is able to detect & track subjects quickly and accurately. What we didn’t like about this is that it doesn't give you as many options to set the focus point types which you’d like and you’d have to adjust to using what’s present in this – which is a learning curve in itself. OM-1 Mark II ISO Performance The OM-1 Mark II by default has an ISO range of 200-25600 but can be expanded to 80-102400. And the one weakness which one could have seen from a mile away – its sensor size – starts to show its head. Despite being low in megapixel count, the smaller pixel size means you start seeing visible noise upwards of ISO 3200 (also depending on the scenario) with photos starting to become less usable above ISO 6400. Highly recommend shooting RAW and cleaning them up in post-processing. But in daylight we didn’t notice much even though our F/4 lens meant pushing the ISO up to freeze action, typical for wildlife. OM-1 Mark II Video Capabilities The OM-1 Mark II is no slouch in video either, offering to shoot at 4K up to 60fps in standard and DCI (C4K) modes. It allows you to shoot in H.264 & H.265 codecs in 8-bit & 10-bit. The OM-1 Mark II restricts 10-bit shooting to H.265 – where you can shoot in OM-Log or HLG. And there are no intermediary codecs like ProRes to shoot with. You win some, you lose some in this department. Video quality is alright straight out of camera, like how you’d expect but for full flexibility we’d recommend shooting in LOG. The star of the show is hands down, its image stabilisation. Paired with a compatible lens, the OM-1 Mark II’s IBIS & digital stabilisation can be customised to your liking to get buttery-smooth footage of any scenario – it’s almost like having a gimbal. However, the autofocus still clearly lags behind even compared to its own photo mode – which makes the biggest difference for a consumer deciding to buy with a camera for hybrid shooting. While it is very close to other brands’ performance when it comes to the specs, but definitely needs more refinement for it to become an actual contender. Verdict At a time where uncertainties in the market are affecting all the camera prices, the OM-1 Mark II is offering a refreshing choice. It’s lighter than competing systems, while offering excellent IBIS, fast autofocus and as a whole system, an array of lens choices. The computational photography modes and IBIS are definitely unbeaten. But there are some areas that OM System needs to address – video being one of them, and with more people including that in their workflow, it’s more of a necessity today than an option. One thing is certain – OM System is here to stay! The biggest question is – would you switch or buy into this system? Perhaps with better pricing and the right push, it does make a very compelling argument. And even with some rough corners, we think this body with its flexibility and the choice of lenses going back to over a decade will definitely serve a lot of photographers well. Stay tuned for a video review of the OM System OM-1 Mark II and more on our YouTube channel. wildlife photography landscape photography

articles.desc: Miniature organs being sent into space for the very first time may soon help scientists understand how spaceflight impacts certain organs and may accelerate aging.
articles.content: Mini organs launching to space may help future astronauts and humans on Earth stay healthy | 19934663 Pick countries on the world map and get breaking news alerts in your browser — free, no app. Miniature organs being sent into space for the very first time may soon help scientists understand how spaceflight impacts certain organs and may accelerate aging. The mini organs are expected to arrive at the ISS on Thursday. Tuesday, October 13, 2026 12:05PMMiniature organs being sent into space for the very first time may soon help scientists understand how spaceflight impacts certain organs and may accelerate aging. In a joint effort by researchers from Mount Sinai, NASA and aerospace company Space Tango, these mini organs will be exposed to the increased radiation and microgravity astronauts face in space, especially on long-duration missions. "If people are going to be living and working in space, then we need to understand what's going to happen to them," David Sachs, assistant professor of surgery at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, told ABC News. "But also, because it's interesting as a model of accelerated aging for studying people on Earth. " Miniature organs being sent to space for the first time in a joint effort by researchers from Mount Sinai, NASA and aerospace company Space Tango. The mini organs launched aboard commercial resupply mission CRS-35 on Tuesday morning from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. They are expected to arrive at the International Space Station on Thursday. Astronauts age faster in space because microgravity and radiation exposure negatively affect multiple body systems. The miniature organs offer researchers a unique opportunity to simulate aging in a much shorter period of time to understand disease and develop treatments. "Six months in space ... is equivalent to about 10 to 20 years of aging on Earth," Kevin Costa, associate professor of surgery at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, told ABC News. Sachs and Costa are sending up to 16 miniature hearts to the ISS to test how they respond to electrical signals and monitor how they may react to near-zero gravity.to the ISS in 2023, confirming they could survive in the weightless environment. The technology, which is integrated into a miniature laboratory called CubeLab, was developed by Space Tango and simulates the natural environment in the human body. " slightly bigger than a shoebox, and it is a fully automated, miniaturized system," Gentry Barnett, chief technology officer at Space Tango, told ABC News. As part of the new effort, the team is sending miniature brains, called miBrain, to the ISS. Around the size of a peppercorn, the miBrains reflect models of healthy and diseased brains. By exposing them to the space environment, scientists can see how mini-brains respond and better understand why living in space accelerates aging. Though the mini organs are not full-sized human organs, the researchers say they are good substitutes, cost-effective and don't take up much of the limited space aboard the space station. The microgravity environment uniquely allows researchers to study what happens to humans with a sedentary lifestyle or prolonged bed rest, which isn't easily simulated on Earth, Sachs explained. " translating to stuff in space, but it's also translating back to the research we do in the laboratory to help people with Parkinson's and Alzheimer's disease," Joel Blanchard, associate professor of stem cell biology and regenerative medicine and neuroscience at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, told ABC News. Lisa Carnell, the director of the biological and physical sciences division at NASA, told ABC News that these experiments serve as a starting point for future research beyond low Earth orbit, including to the moon and beyond. articles.title: VERAXA Biotech Presents in vivo Proof-of-Concept Data for BiTAC®-ADC Technology at World ADC Congress
articles.content: VERAXA Biotech Presents in vivo Proof-of-Concept Data for BiTAC®-ADC Technology at World ADC Congress - BioSpace VERAXA Biotech Presents in vivo Proof-of-Concept Data for BiTAC®-ADC Technology at World ADC Congress In vivo data confirm activation of prodrug payload inside tumor cells following systemic administration of BiTAC-ADC molecules leading to potent anti-tumor activity ZURICH, SWITZERLAND – October 13, 2026 -- VERAXA Biotech AG (NASDAQ: VRXA; “VERAXA”), an emerging leader in designing novel cancer therapies, today presented first data validating its novel BiTAC-ADC technology platform at the 17 World ADC Congress in San Diego, CA, USA. The data demonstrate that a systemically applied, single dose of the two-component BiTAC-ADC selectively triggered a tumor-specific response resulting in a significant reduction in tumor volume, while continuing to show differentiated safety features and the potential to overcome systemic toxicity, the primary limitation of current ADCs. data presented at the World ADC Congress showed that treatment with BiTAC-ADCs resulted in strong tumor regression in a xenograft breast cancer model even at a single dose of 3 mg/kg. As intended, BiTAC-ADCs utilizing one non-targeted component, thereby only delivering one component to the tumor, showed no significant effect. A control ADC, engineered by VERAXA using the same conjugation and linker-payload technology and with the same drug-antibody ratio (DAR) as its BiTAC-ADC counterpart, performed similarly. In the BiTAC-ADC treatment arm, no decrease in body weight could be observed. “These novel datasets on the BiTAC-ADC platform underline the rapid progress our team has made in demonstrating the potentially transformative safety benefits of BiTAC-ADCs compared to conventional ADCs,” said Christoph Erkel, Ph.D., Chief Scientific Officer at VERAXA. “While BiTAC-TCEs remain our priority, the rapid validation of our BiTAC-ADC concept bodes well for establishing a second pillar in our R&D and partnering strategy towards safer drugs for solid tumor patients.” “Demonstrating that BiTAC-ADCs can reach the tumor site following intravenous administration, induce a specific effect only upon arrival of both BiTAC components, and shrink the tumor in a living organism is a significant platform milestone and validates its underlying concept,” added Paul Sauter, Ph.D., Senior Director and Department Head ADC Tech & Chemistry at VERAXA. The poster presented at the World ADC congress also expanded on previously published studies and shows that BiTAC-ADCs can discriminate between cancer and healthy cells, require both BiTAC-ADC constructs to be co-targeted to the tumor site and do not release active toxins in the periphery. The BiTAC-ADC concept was also successfully evaluated across a wide range of cancer cell lines and against several validated ADC targets. Taken together, the data sets underline the potential for this novel therapeutic concept with comparable efficacy to a conventional ADC, but a mechanistically highly differentiated safety profile. The BiTAC therapeutic strategy is designed to unlock a new level of precision in cancer treatment via dual-targeting using two complementary precursors and enabling a tumor-restricted activation of the desired therapeutic effect. Applied to the development of antibody drug conjugates (ADCs), the technology delivers a systemically inactive prodrug and a cell-impermeable proactivator through two separate antibodies, each addressing a defined tumor-associated antigen. While the single BiTAC-ADC precursors are therefore not toxic by design, the selective internalization of both components into the same cancer cell leads to dose-dependent cytotoxicity. The data poster presented will be made available on the At VERAXA, we are building a premier engine for the discovery and development of next-generation antibody-based therapeutics, including bispecific T cell engagers, bispecific ADCs and other innovative formats. articles.title: How SIP Calculator Helps Estimate Potential Investment Growth?
articles.desc: Learn how an SIP calculator helps estimate potential investment growth based on your monthly contribution, expected rate of return, and investment tenure to support informed financial planning.
articles.content: How SIP Calculator Helps Estimate Potential Investment Growth? How SIP Calculator Helps Estimate Potential Investment Growth? How SIP Calculator Helps Estimate Potential Investment Growth? Learn how an SIP calculator helps estimate potential investment growth based on your monthly contribution, expected rate of return, and investment tenure to support informed financial planning. Investors can use SIP calculators to compare monthly contributions, investment periods and assumed returns while planning financial goals | Representational Image You may know how much you can set aside each month but still find it hard to picture what those contributions might amount to over several years. An SIP calculator can turn an amount and a time period into an illustration. It shows how regular contributions and an assumed potential rate of return affect a projected value. That number is a planning aid. Mutual fund values can change, and the actual amount at the end of your investment period may differ from the illustration. A typical calculator asks for a contribution amount, how often you plan to contribute, how long you plan to continue and an assumed annual rate. Check which inputs the tool uses before reading its result. Suppose you enter ₹2,500 a month for eight years. If all 96 instalments are made, your contributions would total ₹2.4 lakh. The calculator then applies your assumed rate to illustrate a potential future value. It may show the contribution total separately, helping you distinguish the money you plan to put in from any projected potential growth. The figures shown are for illustrative purpose only The calculation generally assumes that instalments happen on schedule. A missed or delayed contribution changes the amount and timing of money invested. Treat the output as an illustration of the inputs you entered, not as a record of what has already happened. Start with an amount that fits your budget If you plan to invest in an SIP, you could begin with an amount you think you can contribute regularly without relying on money needed for other expenses. The calculator may display a higher projected value when you increase the instalment, but that does not make the larger amount suitable for you. Try comparing two contribution amounts while keeping the period and assumed rate the same. The difference can show how much the projection depends on what you put in. This may help you consider whether an increase could fit your budget, or whether the original amount is more manageable. cannot decide how much you should invest. For the same instalment and a positive assumed rate, a longer period will usually produce a larger projected figure because it includes more contributions and more time for potential investment growth. Yet a 15-year estimate will not answer a question about money you may need in five years. Consider using the period that matches your goal date. The cost of a future goal may also change. If you are planning for an expense several years away, today’s price may not be the amount you eventually need. A calculator focused on contributions may not account for that change. You can keep the goal estimate separate and revisit it as the date approaches. Time also affects which fund may be suitable. An SIP is a way of contributing, not an investment type by itself. Each fund has its own risks, and its value may rise or fall regardless of how regularly you invest. The rate is an input you choose, not a forecast of a fund’s potential return. Try more than one assumption and observe how the projected value changes. If your plan appears to work only at the highest rate, consider what you could adjust without depending on that outcome.
